title: Ἀηδὼν καὶ χελιδών
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 9. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἀηδόνι συνεβούλευε χελιδὼν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις εἶναι ὁμόροφον καὶ σύνοικον ὡς αὐτή.
sentences.tr: Aēdoni synebouleue chelidōn tois anthrōpois einai homorophon kai synoikon hōs autē.
sentences.l: To a nightingale a swallow was giving advice, to be under-the-same-roof with men and a house-mate, as she herself was.
sentences.i: A swallow was urging a nightingale to live under men's roofs and share their houses, as she did herself.
sentences.n: συμβουλεύω takes the dative of the person advised (Ἀηδόνι, first word for emphasis) and an infinitive of the advice. ὁμόροφος is a compound, “of the same roof” (ὁμός + ὄροφος), and holds the whole contrast: swallows nest in houses, nightingales in the wild.

sentences.t: Ἡ δὲ εἶπεν· « Οὐ θέλω τὴν λύπην τῶν παλαιῶν μου συμφορῶν μεμνῆσθαι, καὶ διὰ τοῦτο τὰς ἐρήμους οἰκῶ. »
sentences.tr: Hē de eipen: « Ou thelō tēn lypēn tōn palaiōn mou symphorōn memnēsthai, kai dia touto tas erēmous oikō. »
sentences.l: And she said: « I do not wish to remember the grief of my old misfortunes, and for this reason I dwell in the desolate places. »
sentences.n: The old misfortune is the myth the fable expects you to know: the Athenian sisters Prokne and Philomela, whose story ends in a murdered child and their transformation into swallow and nightingale (which sister becomes which varies with the teller). μεμνῆσθαι is a perfect infinitive with present force, “to hold in mind, remember.” τὰς ἐρήμους, “the deserted places,” is a feminine adjective with χώρας understood.

sentences.t: [Ὅτι] τὸν λυπηθέντα ἔκ τινος τύχης καὶ τὸν τόπον φεύγειν ἐθέλειν ἔνθα ἡ λύπη συνέβη.
sentences.tr: [Hoti] ton lypēthenta ek tinos tychēs kai ton topon pheugein ethelein entha hē lypē synebē.
sentences.l: [That] the one grieved by some chance wishes to flee even the place where the grief came about.
sentences.i: A man grieved by some mischance will shun even the place where the grief befell him.
sentences.n: Chambry brackets [Ὅτι] as a later addition; without it the moral stands as a bare accusative-and-infinitive (τὸν λυπηθέντα … ἐθέλειν) hanging on an unspoken “the story shows…”, which is why the English needs a word supplied. καί here is “even” — not merely the company but the place itself. τύχη is chance, and as often here it is chance for the worse.
